newsitem.title: USA: CME lumber closes mixed, nearbys slip again late.
newsitem.headline: CME lumber closes mixed, nearbys slip again late.

text.p: CME lumber futures recovered from sharp early losses after midsession, but nearbys slipped again late as profit taking developed and long liquidation continued in September, traders said.
Indications that cash spruce prices remained strong pared almost all of the early break before fresh profit taking developed late, they said.

Initial carryover pressure followed the sharp break in prices Friday. Futures fell in the aftermath of Hurricane Fran which produced less-than-expected damage. Some selling was also linked to reports of slowing cash trade, they said.

Private sources noted that although some types of wood were showing reduced demand, cash spruce remained strong with prices in the $430 to $435 per tbf area. Some mill order files were sold out into the first week of October, they said.
Lumber closed $3.70 per tbf lower to $4.50 higher with only September and November off. September was down most at $418.50 and November was off $3.50 at $384.50 per tbf.
